title: 3-Read Friday #44: Routines, Priorities, and Theories
author: Craig Barton
summary: As the new school year begins, Barton's picks all circle the theme of getting September right. He opens with a Teach Like a Champion video showing two teachers rehearsing how they will introduce a Turn and Talk routine, framing the start of the year as the ideal moment to establish or tighten classroom routines. He follows with Peter Foster's post aimed at new teachers on setting first-weeks priorities, noting that although it targets the newly qualified, he thinks there's value in it for teachers at any career stage. He closes with Michael Pershan's analysis of why bestselling education books like Building Thinking Classrooms and Carol Dweck's Mindset become so popular, which Barton flags as offering a useful note of caution alongside the enthusiasm.
points: Barton treats the start of the school year as the natural moment to establish or reset classroom routines, using the TLAC rehearsal video as the model.
He recommends Foster's new-teacher post to his whole readership, not just NQTs, arguing the first-weeks priorities apply across experience levels.
He flags Pershan's critique of why big theory-plus-technique education books go viral as a useful caution against over-adopting trendy frameworks wholesale.
The issue as a whole is organised around September as a reset point: routines, priorities, and a critical eye on which new ideas are worth adopting.
quotes: The start of the academic year is the ideal time to introduce or tighten up routines with students.
